newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore gas oil, fuel oil fall on poor demand.
newsitem.headline: Singapore gas oil, fuel oil fall on poor demand.

text.p: Singapore oil product prices fell across the barrel on weak crude values with gas oil and fuel oil sliding $1.00 as sellers emerged but buyers stayed away, traders said on Tuesday.
They said Indonesia was expected to seek February barrels only next week.
With the scheduled one-month shutdown of the 120,000-bpd Dumai refinery in February, traders expect Indonesia to buy substantial volumes of gas oil for that month.
But with China taking a pause and South Korea expected to sell larger volumes, prices are expected to come under intense pressure, traders said.

Much lower gas oil offers were seen with a major offering a 30,000-tonne cargo loading Jan 29-Feb 2 at $29.20 a barrel, and a Feb 7-11 at $29. Another major offered 30,000 tonnes Jan 30-Feb 3 at $29.25 a barrel or 25 cents premium to spot Singapore quotes, fob basis.
The lowest traded level on Friday was $30.65 a barrel. Taiwan sold one gas oil cargo at $29.55 a barrel for Jan 26-Feb 15 lifting fob and might sell at least another cargo, traders said.
Naphtha plunged with overnight losses in the West. February swaps fell by 50 cents to $24.20/$24.50. But prices were still near post-Gulf war highs on tight supplies.

Traders saw support because several refineries were planning March turnarounds. Demand was seen for full-range rather than light cargoes as BTX was stronger than ethylene. Sellers put wet gasoline premium around $2/bbl over Singapore naphtha quotes.
